newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Danube rises in Hungary but no danger seen.
newsitem.headline: Danube rises in Hungary but no danger seen.

text.p: Water levels along the Hungarian section of the river Danube continued to rise on Monday but were not expected to reach dangerous levels, the authorities said.

Hungary's Flood Control Centre told the Hungarian news agency MTI the river had risen 60 cm (two feet) overnight and a full flood alert had been issued at the wetlands of Szigetkoz, which straddle the border with Slovakia.
Lower-level alerts were issued further downriver as far as Budapest while ferry services between the city of Esztergom and the Slovak town of Sturovo were to be suspended on Tuesday.
The centre said earlier the Danube was expected to rise by a daily 70 cm (just of two feet) on Monday and Tuesday in Budapest and would peak at 710 cm (23 feet) on Wednesday.
Such levels involve the closing of sections of Budapest's waterside highways from Monday but pose no threat of flooding to the capital.
The stretch of Danube river in Austria from the German bordertown of Passau through to Linz was reopened to shipping early on Monday morning, Austrian river police said.
However, roughly 50 km (30 miles) of the Danube between the Slovak border and the Freudenau lock east of Vienna remained closed.
The stretch is expected to be reopened by the end of Monday.
Danube shipping was suspended in Austria on Sunday as days of torrential rain in central and eastern Europe took their toll.
